primary.title: Missile hits Riyadh's international airport
primary.description: A projectile struck a passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia on Sunday, a day after a missile strike killed 12 and injured more than 300 people at the site.A Saudi-led coalition fighting Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen informed AP about the situation, however, the authorities did not release any official statament on the latest strike.Also read: Tension spikes in West Asia as Saudi coalition threatens retaliation after deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh airportThe missile strike on Sunday appeared to hit the same complex housing passenger terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights.The sharp escalation in the latest front in the Iran war threatens to draw in greater US military involvement as American President Donald Trump said that he is weighing joining the fight against the rebels.The strike on Sunday occurred as the Riyadh Airport remained closed and authorities moved schools in the Saudi capital online.11 Indians injured in Saturday attacks in Saudi ArabiaThe Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia informed that 11 Indians got injured in the attacks on Riyadh airport on Saturday."Embassy of India, Riyadh has been following up on the dastardly attack on Riyadh airport yesterday in which 12 people unfortunately died and more than 300 were injured. It is learnt that 11 Indians are among those injured in the attack," it said in a statemant.The Indian Embassy has been in touch with local authorities to enquire about their well being and officials have also reached out to the hospital authorities.We will provide further updates as they become available, it said.Also read: Riyadh airport operations suspended for another 24 hours— IndianEmbRiyadh (@IndianEmbRiyadh) External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar reiterated that the Indian Embassy is doing everything necessary in this difficult situation.

articles.title: Missile hits Riyadh's international airport
articles.description: A projectile struck a passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia on Sunday, a day after a missile strike killed 12 and injured more than 300 people at the site.A Saudi-led coalition fighting Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen informed AP about the situation, however, the authorities did not release any official statament on the latest strike.Also read: Tension spikes in West Asia as Saudi coalition threatens retaliation after deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh airportThe missile strike on Sunday appeared to hit the same complex housing passenger terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights.The sharp escalation in the latest front in the Iran war threatens to draw in greater US military involvement as American President Donald Trump said that he is weighing joining the fight against the rebels.The strike on Sunday occurred as the Riyadh Airport remained closed and authorities moved schools in the Saudi capital online.11 Indians injured in Saturday attacks in Saudi ArabiaThe Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia informed that 11 Indians got injured in the attacks on Riyadh airport on Saturday."Embassy of India, Riyadh has been following up on the dastardly attack on Riyadh airport yesterday in which 12 people unfortunately died and more than 300 were injured. It is learnt that 11 Indians are among those injured in the attack," it said in a statemant.The Indian Embassy has been in touch with local authorities to enquire about their well being and officials have also reached out to the hospital authorities.We will provide further updates as they become available, it said.Also read: Riyadh airport operations suspended for another 24 hours— IndianEmbRiyadh (@IndianEmbRiyadh) External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar reiterated that the Indian Embassy is doing everything necessary in this difficult situation.
